modelingNotes: Camp North End: the Gama Goat Building — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-cne-gama-goat.ts

The extension the Army added to its Building No. 6 some time before 1955, running north-east from `clt-cne-1701-n-graham` between the railway and North Graham Street; 1801 N. Graham Street. Unlike the brick warehouses it is a steel shed clad in corrugated metal, here painted charcoal, with one long clerestory monitor down its spine instead of monitors across it. A box 41 × 183 m; along the street its wall stands back under the deep eaves of the roof on steel posts and braces; a loading platform under a canopy along the railway side; open canopies over platforms at both ends, the north-east end cut on the diagonal.
Identity: the long charcoal shed with its raised spine monitor and the deep dark eaves along North Graham Street.

Evidence: - OSM: the outline way/632256525 ("Gama Goat Building", height 8) and its 13 parts: the spine monitor in two lengths way/835812875, 835812880 (gabled, height 10.1/10.2), the side roofs 835812876, 835812878, 835812879, 835812881 (7.2), the railway platform 835812877, the end platforms 835812873, 836935996 and the strip between the monitor lengths 835812885 (1), the north-east canopy 835812883 (min_height 4.9), the small blocks 835812874 (4) and 835842063 (2). - Lidar, USGS 3DEP NC Phase 4 Mecklenburg 2016, 1 m (measured, NAVD88): ground 228.0–228.7 (y = 0 is 228.0); side roofs 235.9–236.4 (8.1 m); the monitor 238.8–239.0 (10.9 m), flat to within 0.2 m, so drawn with a flat lid; the strip between its two lengths 236.4 (no monitor there); the south-west canopy 235.3 (7.3 m); the railway canopy 234.3 (6.3 m); the north-east canopy 234.1 (6.1 m). - C-M Historic Landmarks Commission survey report (2017, landmarkscommission.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Ford-Motor-Co-Plant-SR.pdf), Buildings Nos. 4–6 (published): No. 6 "expanded some time before 1955; this new addition contains the same steel framing and concrete floors, but ... is sided with aluminum or vinyl and has a 6-foot single monitor that runs the rest of the length". - Mecklenburg County tax parcel 07903C99 (CAMP GAMA GOAT PROPERTY OWNER LP). Camp North End leasing brochure (2021, camp.nc): "Gama Goat Building", 85,000 sq ft. OSM name and address. - Mapillary photos 337256698419883 and 296443739342389 (aftcpics471, 2022-04-21, CC BY-SA 4.0), from North Graham Street looking north-east along the street front: charcoal corrugated walls with tall windows, set back under deep eaves with a pale grey fascia, carried on dark steel posts and knee braces, the framing open at the north-east end, a pale concrete base. - USGS NAIP orthophoto (public domain): white side roofs, the grey spine.

Estimated: the eaves' depth (3.5 m, the street wall drawn at x = 20.5 inside OSM's 24.1 outline), the post spacing, window sizes and spacing (photo-scaled); the railway and end faces, unphotographed, are given doors and a few windows. The wall colour is pulled to charcoal #5b6067 from the photos' near-black.
Frame and kit: `clt-cne-301-camp-road.ts`. y along the long axis (bearing 39.62°), placement bearing 39.62; origin at the outline's centroid, lng −80.8316634, lat 35.2459136.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "clt-cne-gama-goat", model "clt-cne-gama-goat"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/a1974bbf738c6994edbe99a7a61818b9d69da9e0/generators/clt-cne-gama-goat.ts. Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
